arguments.summary: A Golden Ticket attack was confirmed originating from host 10.0.5.14, which performed a DCSync operation (Event ID 4662) against domain controller 10.0.1.10 to extract the krbtgt account hash. This compromise allows the adversary to forge Kerberos Ticket Granting Tickets (TGTs) for any user, rendering all domain authentication credentials untrustworthy. The attack chain began with a compromised host (WS-FIN-042, 10.0.5.42) exhibiting Cobalt Strike beaconing, followed by lateral movement and privilege escalation. Multiple containment actions were denied due to policy or parameter errors, delaying response. The source of the DCSync was misidentified initially as 10.0.5.14, but logs indicate the true source was WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The 10.0.1.10 IP is incorrectly associated with a low-criticality IT workstation (WS-IT-101), which requires CMDB correction.

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_HTTP {
    meta:
        description = "Detects HTTP traffic patterns associated with Cobalt Strike beacons"
        author = "SOC Team"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $http_get = /GET \/[a-z]{4} HTTP\/1\.1/ 
        $http_host = /Host: [0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}/ 
        $http_useragent = /User-Agent: Mozilla\/5\.0 \(Windows NT [\d.]+\) AppleWebKit\/\d+.\d+ \(KHTML, like Gecko\) Chrome\/\d+.\d+.\d+.\d+ Safari\/\d+.\d+/ 
        $http_accept = /Accept: \*\// 
    condition:
        all of ($http_*)
}

rule CobaltStrike_Beacon_Dynamic_Loader {
    meta:
        description = "Detects runtime injection of Cobalt Strike beacon via rundll32 or similar loaders"
        author = "SOC Team"
        reference = "MITRE ATT&CK T1218.011"
        tlp = "amber"
    strings:
        $beacon_config = { 2E 72 63 64 2E 64 61 74 } // ".rcd.dat" - common beacon artifact
        $injection_api = "VirtualAlloc" wide ascii
        $loader_pattern = "rundll32" nocase
    condition:
        $loader_pattern and $injection_api and $beacon_config
}

The exfiltration source (10.0.7.50) showed no active malicious processes during EDR check.

arguments.summary: A high-severity data exfiltration attempt was detected from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42) using DNS tunneling over domain c2.evil-example.com. The host exhibited Cobalt Strike beaconing behavior, attempted Kerberos TGT requests, and lateral movement via SMB. The source of the initial alert (10.0.7.50) was a benign IT workstation, while the true compromised asset was identified as WS-FIN-042. Containment actions included firewall rule deployment to block tunneling on port 99999 and isolation of the infected host. The endpoint was scanned and cleaned, and user credentials were reset.

WS-FIN-042 isolated from network; full EDR scan initiated and malicious artifacts removed.

arguments.summary: Unauthorized access incident initiated through a compromised service account (svc_unrelated_service) with excessive privileges. The attacker used stolen credentials of user j.martinez to establish a remote session from an anomalous geolocation (Russia). Initial access was achieved via a phishing campaign delivering a malicious PowerShell payload, leading to Cobalt Strike beaconing from host WS-FIN-042 (10.0.5.42). The attacker pivoted using the overprivileged service account to access the HR database at 10.0.8.200. Despite detection of C2 traffic and suspicious behaviors, containment actions (account disable, firewall block) were denied due to lack of approval workflow integration.

        description = "Detects PowerShell using Invoke-Expression with remote content"

    condition:
        $iex and $webclient
}
